summary: Eight new sources include Portuguese Amazonian scholarship, French criticism, comparative Confucian and Indian arguments, Nahua textual mediation and reader testimony. Western category imposition and collective authorship remain explicit issues.
next: Broaden independent domains and original-language evidence; expand literary-fiction corpus substantially.

sources.title: What is the cure for the West’s individualist worldview?
sources.note: Compares Rosemont, Ames, Rošker, Ivanhoe and Puett on relational selves; distinguishes expanding individuality through relationships from erasing it, and ordinary ritual from political feasibility.
sources.location: Modern Confucian books and practical limits
sources.limits: Comparative advocacy, not a survey of all Confucian traditions.

sources.title: Life on the slippery Earth
sources.note: Purcell reconstructs socially supported virtue from Florentine Codex book six, distinguishing a worthwhile life from guaranteed happiness; identifies mediation through colonial-era recording.
sources.limits: Collective discourses cannot be assigned to an invented single philosopher; colonial compilation requires provenance care.

sources.title: L’intelligence du méchant

sources.title: Sobre a possibilidade de uma filosofia amazônica
sources.note: Develops dialogue with Yepamahsã thought through Barreto and Maia while warning that calling ritual knowledge Western ethics or art repeats ethnophilosophical distortions; names Kopenawa’s autoethnography.
sources.limits: Do not automatically label every knowledge specialist a philosopher; book and individual eligibility remain questions.

sources.title: Favourite philosophy book which changed everything for you?

sources.title: Le divin avant les dieux
sources.note: Lebiez discusses Zambrano’s philosophical-poetic account of the divine preceding particular gods; reports delayed French reception and the reading difficulty of its religious and non-systematic language.
sources.limits: French reception differs from Spanish influence; poetic philosophy is not automatically literary fiction.
